item.vignette: Airway smooth-muscle cells are exposed to ensifentrine. Intracellular cyclic nucleotide concentrations rise despite unchanged adenylyl cyclase and guanylyl cyclase activity.
item.lead_in: Which direct enzymatic action best explains this finding?
item.tested_construct: Dual inhibition of PDE3 and PDE4 with accumulation of intracellular cyclic nucleotides
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Ensifentrine directly inhibits PDE3 and PDE4. PDE3 hydrolyzes cAMP and can also hydrolyze cGMP, whereas PDE4 hydrolyzes cAMP; inhibition therefore increases intracellular cAMP and/or cGMP.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Ensifentrine inhibits PDE3 and PDE4.
distractor_explanations.B: Guanylyl cyclase activation would increase cGMP synthesis rather than reduce cyclic-nucleotide breakdown.
distractor_explanations.C: PDE5 selectively regulates cGMP and is not the direct target pair of ensifentrine.
distractor_explanations.D: Adenylyl cyclase activation increases cAMP synthesis but is not ensifentrine pharmacology.
distractor_explanations.E: Protein kinase A is downstream of cAMP and is not directly inhibited by ensifentrine.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibition as a mechanism that raises intracellular cyclic nucleotides in COPD therapy.

item.vignette: A patient with classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency receives crinecerfont. Pituitary corticotropin-releasing factor signaling is reduced, and adrenal androgen excess improves without correcting the CYP21A2 defect.
item.lead_in: Which hormone decreases most directly because of this drug?
item.tested_construct: CRF1 receptor antagonism in the pituitary with reduced ACTH secretion
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Crinecerfont selectively antagonizes CRF type 1 receptors in the pituitary. Blocking CRF1 signaling reduces ACTH secretion, thereby decreasing ACTH-driven adrenal androgen production in classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

distractor_explanations.A: Aldosterone is not the direct pituitary output controlled by CRF1.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. CRF1 antagonism reduces pituitary ACTH secretion.
distractor_explanations.C: Cortisol synthesis remains limited by the underlying steroidogenic enzyme defect.
distractor_explanations.D: Renin is regulated mainly by renal perfusion, sodium delivery, and sympathetic tone.
distractor_explanations.E: Angiotensin II is generated through the renin-angiotensin system, not directly by pituitary CRF1 signaling.

explanation.educational_objective: Link pituitary CRF1 antagonism with reduced ACTH drive and reduced adrenal androgen production in classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

item.vignette: Desmoid tumor cells are exposed to nirogacestat. Surface Notch receptors remain present, but generation of the transcriptionally active intracellular Notch fragment is reduced.
item.lead_in: Which molecular step is most directly inhibited?

options.A: Binding of Notch ligand to the extracellular receptor
options.B: ADAM-family cleavage of the Notch ectodomain
options.D: Ubiquitination of the Notch intracellular domain

item.tested_construct: Gamma-secretase inhibition that blocks proteolytic activation of the Notch receptor
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Nirogacestat is a gamma-secretase inhibitor that blocks proteolytic activation of the Notch receptor. This prevents generation of the active Notch signaling fragment that would otherwise promote downstream transcription.

distractor_explanations.A: Ligand binding is upstream and is not the direct inhibited step.
distractor_explanations.B: The direct labeled target is gamma secretase rather than the initial ectodomain cleavage step.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Nirogacestat blocks gamma-secretase-dependent proteolytic activation of Notch.
distractor_explanations.D: Ubiquitination is not the direct pharmacologic target.
distractor_explanations.E: Beta-catenin degradation belongs to a different signaling pathway.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize gamma-secretase-dependent proteolytic activation as a druggable step in Notch signaling.

item.vignette: A patient with postpartum depression receives a 14-day course of zuranolone. Shortly after dosing, central inhibitory neurotransmission is enhanced and psychomotor performance may be impaired.
item.lead_in: Which receptor is directly positively modulated by this drug?
item.tested_construct: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Zuranolone is a neuroactive steroid whose therapeutic action in postpartum depression is thought to be related to positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors, thereby enhancing inhibitory GABAergic signaling.

distractor_explanations.A: NMDA receptors mediate excitatory glutamatergic transmission and are not the direct target.
distractor_explanations.B: GABA-B receptors are metabotropic and are not the labeled receptor target of zuranolone.
distractor_explanations.C: 5-HT1A agonism is a serotonergic mechanism used by other agents.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Zuranolone positively modulates GABA-A receptors.
distractor_explanations.E: D2 antagonism is not the mechanism of zuranolone.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize neuroactive-steroid positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors as the direct pharmacologic action of zuranolone.

item.vignette: B lymphocytes from a patient with activated PI3K-delta syndrome are exposed to leniolisib. Akt phosphorylation decreases and abnormal lymphocyte activation is reduced.
item.lead_in: Which intracellular lipid second messenger decreases most directly?
item.tested_construct: PI3K-delta inhibition with reduced PIP3 production and downstream Akt signaling
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Leniolisib selectively inhibits PI3K-delta by blocking its active binding site. PI3K-delta normally generates phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3), which activates downstream Akt/mTOR signaling; inhibition therefore lowers PIP3 and pAkt activity.

distractor_explanations.A: PIP2 is the substrate used to generate PIP3 rather than the direct product that falls.
distractor_explanations.B: DAG is produced by phospholipase C signaling, not directly by PI3K-delta.
distractor_explanations.C: IP3 is also generated by phospholipase C and is not the direct lipid product of PI3K-delta.
distractor_explanations.D: cAMP is regulated by adenylyl cyclase and phosphodiesterases, not directly by PI3K-delta.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. PI3K-delta inhibition reduces production of PIP3 and downstream Akt signaling.

explanation.educational_objective: Link PI3K-delta inhibition with reduced PIP3 generation and decreased Akt/mTOR pathway activity in activated PI3K-delta syndrome.
